lines.text: Homer's Iliad never mentions Achilles' heel.
The famous story, where his mother dips baby Achilles in the River Styx, holding him by the heel, comes from a Roman poet named Statius.
That's around eight hundred years after Homer.
In the Iliad, Achilles isn't magically protected at all. He even gets wounded by a spear, in the arm.
And the poem ends before he dies. Later stories say Paris shot him with an arrow, guided by the god Apollo.
Today, an Achilles' heel means a fatal weakness, and the tendon in your heel is named after him.
